validity.researcher_notes:
Checked the geometry directly against this repo's own Natural Earth boundary data (data/boundaries/ne_50m_admin_0_countries.shp for the country check, data/boundaries/ne_10m_admin_1_states_provinces.shp to identify which Russian region): the drawn straight line from (59.14E,50.16N) to (63.64E,53.22N) genuinely intersects Russian territory for ~117 km across two segments (~59.69-59.86E and ~60.12-61.09E). Sampling points along that intersection against the admin-1 layer places them inside 'Orenburg, Russia' every time -- this is the real, well-documented southward salient of Orenburg Oblast (near Kvarkeno) that pokes into the gap between Aktobe and Kostanay regions, not a Natural Earth coarseness artifact (checked at 1:10m admin-1 resolution, not just 1:50m country outline).

However, every independent source on this project (the TEO document and four press sources, all already cited in the prior leg's P6834.json) describes it as a strictly domestic Kazakhstan undertaking -- KS-14 compressor station (Aktobe region, on the Bukhara-Ural trunk) to Kostanay, built by QazaqGaz + Qatar's UCC Holding for Kazakh regional gas supply. None mentions any Russian-side routing, land acquisition, or cross-border permitting, which a project actually crossing into Russia would require and which Kazakh regional press covering this project in detail (2023-2025) would very likely have reported. My read: the route in this repo is a straight-line placeholder between two endpoint coordinates (consistent with RouteAccuracy='very low (straight line/schematic)' for a still-unbuilt pipeline), and a straight line between two points in Kazakhstan happens to clip a real Russian salient that any actual engineered corridor would obviously route around. This is a route-drawing artifact, not a CountriesOrAreas data defect -- recommend leaving CountriesOrAreas as Kazakhstan-only and revisiting the route itself (not the country field) once real alignment/TEO map data can be digitized.
